title: Binary Tree Right Side View
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the right side of it. Return the values of the nodes you can see, ordered from top to bottom — that is, the rightmost node at each depth level.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to compute the right side view.

examples.explanation: From the right, you see 1 at depth 0, 3 at depth 1, and 4 at depth 2.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 100]
hints: This is a level-order BFS problem in disguise — for each level, the last node processed left-to-right is exactly the one visible from the right.
As you do BFS one level at a time, the last value collected during each level's iteration is the answer for that level.

Alternatively with DFS: visit right child before left child, and record the first node you see at each new depth — since right is explored first, that first-seen node per depth is guaranteed to be the rightmost.

solution.approach: Run level-order BFS. For each level, process all nodes at that depth using a queue-size snapshot, and take the value of the last node processed in that level — since nodes are enqueued left-to-right, the last one popped for a level is the rightmost node at that depth. Collect one such value per level.
